title: Ecclesiastes 1:1 (#1)
content:
Of whom was the Teacher a descendant?

The Teacher was a descendant of David, king in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say everything is?

The Teacher says everything is temporary, fleeting, and insubstantial; the whole of it is vapor.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher ask about the benefit of people’s hard work?

He asks what profit people gain from all their hard work.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4 (#1)
content:
What remains forever?

The earth remains forever.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:5 (#1)
content:
What does the sun do every day?

The sun rises and sets, and then hurries back to the place where it will rise again.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:6 (#1)
content:
What does the wind do?

The wind blows toward the south, then turns toward the north; it goes around and around and returns to where it began.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:7 (#1)
content:
Where do all the rivers go?

All the rivers go to the sea, yet the sea never becomes full, and the water keeps flowing.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:8 (#1)
content:
By what is the eye not satisfied?

The eye is not satisfied by what it sees or hears.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:9 (#1)
content:
What will be done?

Whatever has been done in the past is what will be done in the future.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:10 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say about something that seems new?

The Teacher says that whatever seems new already existed long ago, in times before us.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:11 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say about people remembering past generations?

The Teacher says no one remembers the people or events of long ago, and future generations will not be remembered by those who come after them either.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:12 (#1)
content:
Where was the Teacher king?

The Teacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:13 (#1)
content:
To what did the Teacher apply his mind?

The Teacher applied his mind to study and to search out by wisdom everything that is done in the world.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:14 (#1)
content:
To what do all the deeds that are done under the sun amount?

All the deeds that are done under the sun amount to vapor and an attempt to catch the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:15 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say about things that are bent or lacking?

He says that what is bent cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:16 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher say about his wisdom compared to those who ruled in Jerusalem before him?

He said that he had grown and increased in wisdom more than anyone who ruled in Jerusalem before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:17 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher resolve to learn about?

He resolved to learn about wisdom, and also about madness and folly.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:18 (#1)
content:
What increases along with a person’s wisdom and knowledge?

A person who has much wisdom also has much anger, and one who increases knowledge increases pain.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:1 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher discover about pleasure?

The Teacher discovered that pleasure was also only temporary.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:2 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher say about laughter?

The Teacher said that laughter was madness and that pleasure accomplished nothing good.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:3 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher want to find out?

The Teacher wanted to find out what was good for people to do during the days of their lives.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:4 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher build for himself?

The Teacher built houses and planted vineyards for himself.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:5 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher plant in his orchards and parks?

He planted a tree of every kind of fruit in them.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:6 (#1)
content:
Why did the Teacher create pools of water?

The Teacher created pools of water to water a forest of growing trees.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:7 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher own more of than anyone else in Jerusalem?

He owned more cattle and sheep than anyone who had lived in Jerusalem before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:8 (#1)
content:
How did the Teacher find personal pleasure?

The Teacher took many wives and concubines to give himself pleasure.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:9 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher have more of than anyone before him in Jerusalem?

He had more wealth, power, and honor than anyone who had lived in Jerusalem before him, and his wisdom remained with him.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:10 (#1)
content:
In what did the Teacher’s heart rejoice?

The Teacher’s heart rejoiced in all his hard work.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:11 (#1)
content:
Where was there no profit?

There was no profit in any of his labors on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:12 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher turn to consider?

The Teacher turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:13 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher say is more profitable than folly?

The Teacher said that wisdom is more profitable than folly, just as light is better than darkness.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:15 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher realize would happen to him just as it happens to the fool?

The Teacher realized that the same fate, death, would happen to him just as it happens to the fool.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:16 (#1)
content:
Who is not remembered for very long?

The wise person, like the fool, is not remembered for very long.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:17 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher say he hated?

The Teacher said he hated life because the work done under the sun seemed temporary and insubstantial to him.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:18 (#1)
content:
Why did the Teacher hate all his accomplishments?

The Teacher hated all his accomplishments because he would have to leave them to the person who came after him.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:19 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher say no one knows about the person who will come after him?

The Teacher said no one knows whether that person will be wise or foolish.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:20 (#1)
content:
How did the Teacher’s heart feel about his work?

The Teacher’s heart began to despair over all the work that he did.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:21 (#1)
content:
What happens to what a wise, skillful person has worked for?

He must leave it to someone who did not work for it.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:22 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher ask about all of a person’s hard work?

He asks what lasting benefit a person gets from all his hard work.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:23 (#1)
content:
Why does the hard worker’s heart not find rest at night?

Every day his work causes him pain and stress, so at night his heart does not rest.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:24 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher conclude is the best that people can do?

There is nothing better for anyone than to simply eat and drink and be satisfied with what is good in his work.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:25 (#1)
content:
According to the Teacher, who can eat and enjoy life apart from God?

No one can eat and enjoy life apart from God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:26 (#1)
content:
What does God give to the sinner?

To the sinner, God gives the work of gathering and collecting wealth, which God then gives to someone who pleases him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1 (#1)
content:
For what things is there a season?

There is a season for every matter under the heavens.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:2 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say there is a time for in a person’s life?

There is a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to pull up what was planted.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:3 (#1)
content:
What other times does the Teacher mention for people’s actions?

There is a time to kill and a time to heal, and a time to tear down and a time to build.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:4 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding people’s emotions?

There is a time to weep and a time to laugh, and a time to mourn and a time to dance.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:5 (#1)
content:
What else does the Teacher say there is a time for?

There is a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, and a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:6 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding seeking and keeping?

There is a time to seek and a time to lose, and a time to keep and a time to throw away.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:7 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say there is a time for regarding speaking?

There is a time to be silent and a time to speak.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:8 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say regarding love and war?

There is a time to love and a time to hate, and a time for war and a time for peace.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:9 (#1)
content:
What question does the Teacher ask about a worker’s hard work?

He asks what profit a worker gains from his labor.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:10 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher see?

The Teacher saw the work that God gives to human beings to keep busy with.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:11 (#1)
content:
What did God place in people’s hearts?

God placed eternity in their hearts.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:12 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say is the only good thing for people to do in life?

The Teacher says the only good thing is to rejoice and to do good while they are alive.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:13 (#1)
content:
What is a gift from God?

The ability to eat and drink and the good that comes from one’s work is a gift from God.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:14 (#1)
content:
Why can nothing be added to or taken away from whatever God does?

Nothing can be added to it or taken away from it, because everything God does is unchanging and will last forever.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:15 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say about what happens now and what will happen in the future?

The Teacher says that what happens now has already happened before, and what will happen has already happened too.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:16 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher see in place of justice and equity?

The Teacher saw wickedness in the place of justice and in the place of equity.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:17 (#1)
content:
According to the Teacher, whom will God judge?

The Teacher said God will judge both the equitable and the wicked, because there is a time for every matter and every deed.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:18 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher say God wants to show people about themselves?

The Teacher says God wants to show people that they are like animals.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:19–20 (#1)
content:
How are people like animals?

People and animals’ lives end in the same way—with death.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:21 (#1)
content:
What does the Teacher wonder about the spirits of people and animals?

The Teacher wonders whether the spirit of a person goes upward and the spirit of an animal goes downward to the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:22 (#1)
content:
What is the assignment for each person?

The assignment for each person is to take pleasure in his work.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:1 (#1)
content:
For whom is there no comforter?

There is no comforter for the people who are oppressed.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:2 (#1)
content:
Who did the Teacher praise more than the living?

The Teacher praised the dead who had already died, more than the living who were still alive.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:3 (#1)
content:
Who does the writer say is more fortunate than both the living and the dead?

More fortunate than both the living and the dead is the one who has not yet lived.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:4 (#1)
content:
Why did the Teacher say people work hard and try to succeed?

He said people work hard and try to succeed because they envy their friends.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:5 (#1)
content:
What does the fool do instead of working?

The fool folds his hands and does nothing, and in this way he ruins himself.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:6 (#1)
content:
What is better than being rich with toil and stress-filled labor?

Being contented with little and having peace and quiet is better than having a lot with toil and pursuit of wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:7 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher see again under the sun?

He saw another example of something temporary and meaningless on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:8 (#1)
content:
Who did the Teacher see living alone with no family?

He saw a person who lived alone, had no son or brother, worked endlessly, and was never satisfied with his wealth.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:9–10 (#1)
content:
Why are two people better than one in the case that one falls?

Two people are better than one because if one falls, the other can lift up his friend.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:11 (#1)
content:
How do two people benefit by lying down together?

When two people lie down together, they can keep each other warm.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:12 (#1)
content:
What is not quickly broken?

A three-strand rope is not quickly broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:13 (#1)
content:
What is better than being an old and foolish king?

It is better to be a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:14 (#1)
content:
What did the Teacher imagine about the poor young man?

He imagined that the young man could become king, even though he was born poor.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:15 (#1)
content:
Who did the Teacher see walking around under the sun?

He saw all the living people, along with the one who would succeed the young king.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:16 (#1)
content:
How will the people who live after this king feel about him?

The people who live after him will not rejoice in him.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:1 (#1)
content:
What should people do when they go to the house of God?

They should be careful with their conduct and draw near to listen, for that is better than when fools offer a sacrifice.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:2 (#1)
content:
Why should people let their words be few?

Because God is the eternal God in heaven and people are created by God, so they should think very carefully and not speak rashly or hastily before God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:3 (#1)
content:
What does a fool do when he talks?

A fool talks with many words.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:4 (#1)
content:
What should a person do after he vows a vow to God?

He should fulfill it without delay.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:5 (#1)
content:
What is better for a person to do than to make a vow that he does not carry out?

It is better for a person not to make a vow than to make a vow that he does not carry out.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:6 (#1)
content:
What might God do if a person’s words cause him to sin?

God might become angry and destroy the work of that person’s hands.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:7 (#1)
content:
What should a person do instead of chasing many words and empty things?

He should fear God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:8 (#1)
content:
Why should someone not be astonished when he sees the poor being oppressed and robbed of just and fair treatment?

He should not be astonished because the people who could hold the powerful to account see the injustice and do nothing about it.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:9 (#1)
content:
Who eats from what the fields produce?

Important people and even the king eat from what the fields produce.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:10 (#1)
content:
What happens to a person who loves silver?

A person who loves silver will never be satisfied no matter how much they have.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:11 (#1)
content:
What happens as prosperity increases?

As prosperity increases, so also do the people who consume it.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:12 (#1)
content:
What does not allow a rich person to sleep well?

The wealth of a rich person does not allow him to sleep well.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:13 (#1)
content:
What misfortune did Qoheleth see concerning wealth?

He saw wealth kept by its owner that ended up harming him.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:14 (#1)
content:
What happens when the rich man loses his wealth through misfortune?

When the rich man loses his wealth through misfortune, he has nothing left to give to the son he fathered.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:15 (#1)
content:
How is a man born and how will he leave this life?

A man is born naked from his mother’s womb and possessing nothing, so also, he will leave this life without taking anything he possesses.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:16 (#1)
content:
What profit does a person gain from laboring as if for the wind?

He gains no profit; it is a sickening misfortune.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:17 (#1)
content:
According to the Teacher, how does the man who lost his wealth spend all his days?

He spends all his days in darkness, greatly troubled, sick, and angry.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:18 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth say is good for a person to do?

He said it is good to eat, drink, and find satisfaction in one’s hard work during the life that God has given him.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:19 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth call the ability to enjoy the wealth God gives?

He calls it a gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:20 (#1)
content:
Why does a person not call to mind very often the days of his life?

A person does not call to mind very often the days of his life, because God makes him keep busy with the things that he enjoys doing.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:1–2 (#1)
content:
What misfortune did Qoheleth see?

Qoheleth saw that God might give a person wealth and honor so that he lacks nothing that he desires for himself, but then God gives him no ability to enjoy it. Instead, someone else uses his things.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:3 (#1)
content:
If a man’s heart is not satisfied with good and he is not buried with honor, who is better off than he is?

If a man’s heart is not satisfied with good and he is not buried with honor, then a baby that is born dead is better off than he is.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:4 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say happens to the stillborn child?

Qoheleth says its life is like a mist that fades away, it goes into darkness, and it never receives a name.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:5 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say is true about the stillborn child compared to the unhappy rich man?

Qoheleth says the stillborn child never saw the sun or knew anything, but it has more peace than the unhappy rich man.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:6 (#1)
content:
Even if a man should live for two thousand years but does not learn to enjoy good things, what happens to him?

Even if a man should live for two thousand years but does not learn to enjoy good things, he ends up dying just like everyone else.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:7 (#1)
content:
Though all a man’s work is to fill his mouth, what happens?

Though all a man’s work is to fill his mouth, yet his appetite is not satisfied.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:8 (#1)
content:
According to Qoheleth, what advantage does a wise person have over a fool?

Qoheleth says a wise person has no more advantage than a fool, and a poor person who knows how to live well has no great advantage either.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:9 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say is better than always wanting more?

Qoheleth says it is better to enjoy what a person already has than to always want more, though even this is temporary and insubstantial.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:10 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say about arguing with someone more powerful?

Qoheleth says no one can argue with God, who is more powerful than any person.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:11 (#1)
content:
What happens when many words are spoken?

When many words are spoken, they become more meaningless and do not benefit anyone.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:12 (#1)
content:
Who knows what is good for a person during their short life, according to Qoheleth?

No one knows what is good for a person during their brief life, or what will happen after them.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:1 (#1)
content:
According to Qoheleth, what is better than good oil?

A good name is better than good oil.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:2 (#1)
content:
Why is it better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting?

It is better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting, because everyone dies in the end, and the living should think carefully about this.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:3 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say is better than laughter?

Qoheleth says that grief is better than laughter.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:4 (#1)
content:
Where is the heart of the wise?

The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:5 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say is better than listening to the song of fools?

Listening to the rebuke of a wise person is better than listening to the song of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:6 (#1)
content:
What is the laughter of fools like?

Like the crackling of thorns burning under a pot, so also is the laughter of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:7 (#1)
content:
What makes a wise person foolish?

Oppression makes a wise person foolish, and a bribe corrupts a person’s heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:8 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say is better than the beginning of a thing?

Qoheleth says that the end of a thing is better than its beginning.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:9 (#1)
content:
Why should people not be quick to anger in their spirit?

People should not be quick to anger in their spirit, for anger is a characteristic of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:10 (#1)
content:
What question does Qoheleth say people should not ask?

Qoheleth says people should not ask why the former days were better than the present days.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:11 (#1)
content:
How does Qoheleth describe wisdom in relation to an inheritance?

Qoheleth says wisdom is good, like an inheritance, and gives an advantage to those who are alive.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:12 (#1)
content:
How is wisdom better than money?

Both wisdom and money can provide protection, but the advantage of wisdom is that it prevents foolish actions.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:13 (#1)
content:
Who is able to straighten what God has bent?

No one is able to change what God has done.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:14 (#1)
content:
When times are good, how should people live?

When times are good, people should enjoy them.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:15 (#1)
content:
What happened to some wicked people whom Qoheleth saw?

Some wicked people lived a long time despite their evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:16 (#1)
content:
Why does Qoheleth warn people not to be overly righteous or wise?

Qoheleth warns people not to be overly righteous or overly wise so that they won’t be tempted to think that they can avoid all the painful realities of life through their careful behavior.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:17 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth warn could happen to a person who is very wicked or foolish?

Qoheleth warns that a very wicked or foolish person might die before their time.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:18 (#1)
content:
What will a person who fears God do?

A person who fears God will follow both pieces of this advice—to avoid both wickedness and overly scrupulous righteousness.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:19 (#1)
content:
According to Qoheleth, what makes a wise person stronger than ten rulers in a city?

Wisdom makes a wise person stronger than ten rulers in a city.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:20 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say about whether any person on earth is completely righteous?

Qoheleth says there is no person on earth who does only good and never sins.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:21 (#1)
content:
Why should people not listen to every word that is spoken?

People should not listen to every word that is spoken, because they might hear their servant insulting them.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:22 (#1)
content:
What does a person’s own heart know about how they have treated others?

A person’s own heart knows that they themselves have belittled others many times.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:23 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth say when he tried to become wise?

Qoheleth said he wanted to be wise, but wisdom was far from him.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:24 (#1)
content:
Where is wisdom?

Wisdom is far away and difficult to find.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:25 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth turn his heart to seek?

Qoheleth turned his heart to know and explore wisdom, and to understand wickedness and foolishness.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:26 (#1)
content:
By whom will the sinner be taken?

The sinner will be taken by foolish thinking which is like a woman whose heart is full of snares and nets, and whose hands are chains.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:27 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth say he searched for by considering things one by one?

Qoheleth said he carefully sought to understand the scheme of things, how life works, by considering things one by one.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:28 (#1)
content:
Although Qoheleth continued to search, what did he not find?

Although Qoheleth searched continually for wisdom, he never found it.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:29 (#1)
content:
How did God make humanity, according to what Qoheleth found?

God made humanity upright, but people have sought out many schemes.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:1 (#1)
content:
What is a wise person?

A wise person is someone who is able to understand difficult matters.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:2 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth advise about the king?

Qoheleth advises people to obey the king, because of the oath they swore before God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:3 (#1)
content:
How should people whom the king has ordered to do something wrong respond?

People should not be afraid and should not stand in support of something wrong but should leave the king’s presence immediately in order to protect themselves.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:4 (#1)
content:
Who can question what the king does?

No one can question what the king does, because his word is authoritative.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:5 (#1)
content:
Who avoids harm?

Whoever keeps the king’s commands avoids harm.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:6 (#1)
content:
What exists for every matter?

For every matter there is a proper time and way to do it.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:7 (#1)
content:
What can no one tell a person?

No one can tell a person what will happen in the future.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:8 (#1)
content:
Over what does no one have power?

No one has power over the wind, and no one has power over the day of his death.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:9 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth see about people’s authority over others?

Qoheleth saw that sometimes a person has authority over another and uses it to harm them.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:10 (#1)
content:
By whom were the wicked praised?

The wicked were praised by people in the city where they had done their wicked deeds.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:11 (#1)
content:
What happens when punishment for evil deeds is not given quickly?

When punishment for evil deeds is not given quickly, many people feel tempted to commit evil deeds without fear of consequences

title: Ecclesiastes 8:12 (#1)
content:
Even if a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives for a long time, what will happen to those who fear God?

Even if a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives for a long time, it will be good for those who fear God and honor him.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:13 (#1)
content:
What will happen to the wicked person who does not fear God?

It will not go well for the wicked person, and he will not lengthen his days, because he does not fear God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:14 (#1)
content:
What sometimes happens to righteous people on earth?

Sometimes righteous people seem to experience the bad things that the wicked people deserve.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:15 (#1)
content:
Why does Qoheleth recommend happiness?

Qoheleth recommends happiness because humanity has no better thing to do than to celebrate life and be happy.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:16 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth give his heart to know?

Qoheleth gave his heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:17 (#1)
content:
What can humanity not understand?

Humanity cannot understand everything that God does on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:1 (#1)
content:
Who is in God’s hands?

The righteous and wise people and their work are all in God’s hands.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:2 (#1)
content:
What is the same for everyone?

Everyone dies eventually no matter how they live.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:3 (#1)
content:
Of what are the hearts of human beings full?

The hearts of human beings are full of evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:4 (#1)
content:
Why is it better to be alive than to be dead?

It is better to be alive because, as long as someone is alive, one has hope and the opportunity to enjoy good things.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:5 (#1)
content:
Why do the dead no longer have any reward?

They no longer have any reward because they no longer have anything to gain from what they have done.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:6 (#1)
content:
What died long ago?

The love, hate, and jealousy of the dead perished long ago.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:7 (#1)
content:
Why should a person eat and drink with joy?

A person should eat bread and drink wine with joy because God wants them to do this.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:8 (#1)
content:
What should people always wear?

They should always wear white clothes and have oil on their head.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:9 (#1)
content:
Who should a person enjoy life with?

A person should enjoy life with the wife he loves.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:10 (#1)
content:
Why should people do whatever their hand finds to do?

People should do whatever their hand finds to do, because when they die, they will no longer be able to do anything.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:11 (#1)
content:
What happens to fast, strong, and wise people alike?

Time and unexpected events happen to all of them alike, no matter how fast, strong, or wise they are.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:12 (#1)
content:
In what are human beings snared?

Human beings are snared at a time of misfortune that seizes them unexpectedly.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:13 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth see that seemed great to him?

He saw an example of wisdom that greatly impressed him.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:14 (#1)
content:
What did a great king do to a small city?

He surrounded it and built great siegeworks against it.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:15 (#1)
content:
What happened to the poor wise man, who by his wisdom saved the city?

In a little while, no one remembered the poor wise man, who by his wisdom saved the city.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:16 (#1)
content:
What do people do with the wisdom of a poor person?

No one values the wisdom of a poor person. They despise it and do not listen to his words.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:17 (#1)
content:
Whose words are heeded more than the shouting of a ruler among fools?

The quiet words of wise people are heeded more than the shouting of a ruler among fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:18 (#1)
content:
What is better than weapons of battle?

Wisdom is better than weapons of battle.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:1 (#1)
content:
To what does Qoheleth compare the consequences of a little foolishness?

Qoheleth compares the consequences of a little foolishness to a few flies in perfumer’s oil that cause it to stink.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:2 (#1)
content:
What does the heart of a wise person do compared to the heart of a fool?

The heart of a wise person goes toward the good, but the heart of a fool goes toward evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:3 (#1)
content:
What proves to everyone that a man is a fool?

When a man’s behavior lacks good sense, this proves to everyone that he is a fool.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:4 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say a person should do if the ruler becomes angry with him?

He should not leave his responsibilities, because remaining calm will lessen the ruler’s anger and cause great sins to leave.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:5 (#1)
content:
What misfortune does Qoheleth say he saw under the sun?

He saw a misfortune that is like an unintentional sin that comes from the authority.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:6 (#1)
content:
Who is placed in many high places, and who sits in the lowly place?

Folly is placed in many high places, and rich people sit in the lowly place.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:7 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth see slaves doing?

Qoheleth saw slaves riding on horses like princes and saw princes walking like slaves do.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:8 (#1)
content:
What can happen to someone who digs a pit?

If someone digs a pit, he might fall into the it.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:9 (#1)
content:
What can happen to someone who pulls up stones or splits wood?

Someone who pulls up stones or who splits wood can become injured.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:10 (#1)
content:
What must a man do if he does not sharpen a dull iron blade?

If a man does not sharpen a dull iron blade, he must use more strength.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:11 (#1)
content:
What is of no benefit to the snake charmer?

If a snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gets no benefit.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:12 (#1)
content:
What is a difference between the words of a wise person and the words of a foolish person?

The words of a wise person bring honor to him, but the words of a foolish person will bring harm to him.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:13 (#1)
content:
What are the beginning and the end of a fool’s words?

The beginning of a fool’s words is foolishness, and the end is evil insanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:14 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say a person does not know?

A person does not know what might happen either tomorrow or in the future.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:15 (#1)
content:
What happens to foolish people because of their toil?

Their toil wearies them, so that they do not know how to find their way into their own city.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:16 (#1)
content:
When is there trouble for the land?

There is trouble for the land if its king is a youth and its princes indulge themselves instead of attending to their responsibilities.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:17 (#1)
content:
When is the land blessed?

The land is blessed when its king is a son of nobles and its princes eat at the proper time, with strength and not with drunkenness.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:18 (#1)
content:
What happens to the house because of laziness and idle hands?

Because of laziness the beams of the roof sink, and because of idle hands the house leaks.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:19 (#1)
content:
What does silver do, according to Qoheleth?

Silver is useful for responding to life’s problems.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:20 (#1)
content:
Why should people not belittle a king or a rich person, even in private?

What you say might be repeated in public as if it was carried by a bird.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:1 (#1)
content:
Why should people be generous with what they have?

People should be generous with what they have because others will also be generous to them in return.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:2 (#1)
content:
Why should people give a portion to seven, even eight people?

People should give a portion to seven, even eight people, because they do not know what misfortune will happen on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:3 (#1)
content:
What happens when the clouds are full of rain?

When the clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:4 (#1)
content:
What will the person who keeps waiting for perfect conditions do?

The person who keeps waiting for perfect conditions will delay in fulfilling their responsibilities.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:5 (#1)
content:
What can people not know?

People cannot know the work of God, who does everything.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:6 (#1)
content:
For how long should people plant seed?

People should plant seed in the morning and keep working until the evening.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:7 (#1)
content:
What is good for the eyes to see?

It is good for the eyes to see the sun, because it is good to be alive.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:8 (#1)
content:
What should a man do in all the years that he lives?

He should rejoice in all of them, but he should remember that the difficult days will be many.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:9 (#1)
content:
What should the young man know as he rejoices in his youth?

He should know that God will bring him into judgment for all these things that he does.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:10 (#1)
content:
What should people remove from their heart?

People should remove anger from their heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:1 (#1)
content:
When should people honor and keep in mind their Creator?

People should honor and keep in mind their Creator in the days of their young adulthood.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:3 (#1)
content:
Why will women who grind cease?

The women who grind will cease because they are few.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:4 (#1)
content:
At what sound will a person rise?

A person will rise at the sound of the bird.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:5 (#1)
content:
Where is humanity going?

Humanity is going to their eternal home.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:6 (#1)
content:
What will happen to our lives?

Our lives will end like a silver chain that snaps and like a golden bowl that is broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:7 (#1)
content:
What will happen to our bodies after we die?

Our bodies will decay and return to the earth from where it came.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:8 (#1)
content:
What does Qoheleth say about all of life?

Qoheleth says everything is vapor—temporary and insubstantial.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:9 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth teach the people?

Qoheleth taught the people knowledge.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:10 (#1)
content:
What did Qoheleth seek to find?

Qoheleth sought to find words of pleasure and truth.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:11 (#1)
content:
Like what are the words of the wise?

The words of the wise are like goads, which are sharp tools people use to make animals move.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:12 (#1)
content:
What does much study bring?

Much study brings weariness to the body.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:13 (#1)
content:
What is the end of the matter?

The end of the matter is that people must fear God and keep his commandments.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:14 (#1)
content:
What will God bring into judgment?

God will bring every deed into judgment, including everything hidden, whether good or evil.
